amendments.rule: An English function word the ASV supplies for an adverbial accusative belongs to the noun whose case-function licenses it — *as a bird*, *to your mountain* — and is never `added`. **An appositional or measure nominal the ASV introduces with a supplied preposition is read the same way.** Where a noun or numeral stands in the clause with no preposition and no object marker on it, and the ASV writes an *of* or a *for* before it to state what that nominal contributes, the word is that nominal's own rendering: `אֹרֶךְ חֲמִשָּׁה וְעֶשְׂרִים אֶלֶף` → *the length ... of five and twenty thousand*, `תֹּכֶן אֶחָד` → *of one measure*, `לַאֲחֻזָּה עֶשְׂרִים לְשָׁכֹת` → *for a possession ..., for twenty chambers*, `חַטָּאת שְׂעִיר עִזִּים` → *a he goat ... for a sin offering*. It goes to the word it stands before, which is the noun or numeral opening that phrase, and the unit still heads on the word carrying the lexeme under rules 24 and 31; the supplied preposition is never the head. **A preposition standing elsewhere in the clause that has already taken an English word of its own does not make such a word a surplus.** Rule 52's count governs two English words offered to one morpheme, and here each phrase has a rendering of its own, so a written `לְ` rendered *for a possession* does not silence the *for* the ASV writes before the phrase standing beside it. **But the noun must be present.** Where the ASV supplies the head noun as well as the function word, no morpheme is there to carry either, and the whole supplied phrase is its own `added` unit under rule 30: `חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת בַּחֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת` → *five hundred* ***in length*** *by five hundred* ***in breadth*** supplies both the preposition and the dimension noun in a clause whose Hebrew names neither, exactly as the italic ***reeds*** of `חֲמִשָּׁה וְעֶשְׂרִים אֶלֶף` supplies a measure noun. Test by subtraction as rules 16 and 31 do: drop the English and ask whether a Hebrew noun standing in the clause has lost the relation it bears, or whether what has gone is a noun the Hebrew never wrote. An ASV italic on such a word corroborates it either way and decides nothing, by rule 7.
amendments.why: EZK.45 aligned a supplied *of* or *for* to a bare appositional or measure nominal in 45:1, 45:11, 45:14 and 45:23, and marked the same shape `added` in 45:5 on the strength of an ASV italic. Rule 33 as written says only that such a word is never `added`, without saying which nominal takes it or what happens when the ASV supplies the noun too — and that silence is what let one verse diverge from four. The amendment states the boundary the chapter met on both sides: the word goes to the nominal that is present and heads on the lexeme, while a phrase whose head noun the ASV also supplies (45:2's *in length* and *in breadth*, 45:1's *reeds*) stays `added` under rule 30. The clause about a preposition elsewhere in the clause forecloses the reading that defended the 45:5 error, that לַאֲחֻזָּה's own *for* had already spent the relation.

conventions: A function word the ASV supplies before a bare Hebrew nominal goes to the noun or numeral it stands before under rule 33 and is never `added`, whatever the italic says (rule 7): the *of* of *of five and twenty thousand* (45:1), *of one measure* (45:11) and *of the bath* (45:14), and the *for* of *for twenty chambers* (45:5) and *for a sin offering* (45:23). Only where the ASV supplies the head noun as well is the whole phrase `added`, there being no Hebrew noun in the clause to carry it: the italic *in length* and *in breadth* of 45:2, and the italic *reeds* of 45:1.

אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה → *the Lord Jehovah* is divided the same way at every occurrence (45:9, 45:15, 45:18): the supplied *the* joins the title under rule 15, אֲדֹנָי takes *Lord*, the possessive suffix is `unrepresented` under rule 22, and יְהוִה takes *Jehovah*. This is the source of the four Sp1cs disagreements with BSB, which renders the suffix.

In the date formulae the ordinal or numeral is what the ASV determines. Where the Hebrew writes no יוֹם or חֹדֶשׁ, the italic noun joins the ordinal's own unit — *the first month* (45:18, 45:21), *the seventh day* (45:20), *the seventh month* (45:25) — and where יוֹם is written it takes *day* while the numeral keeps only the supplied *the*: *the fourteenth day* (45:21), *the fifteenth day* (45:25). A compound numeral the ASV renders by one English word shares a unit under rule 30, including its waw where one stands: *fifteen* (45:12), *fourteenth* (45:21), *fifteenth* (45:25).

Rule 31's subtraction test placed the head on the lexeme-bearing word in every multi-word rendering of a single substantive, and that word is not always the same part of speech. It is the attributive in קֹדֶשׁ → *holy portion* and *holy place*, חַטָּאת → *sin offering*, מִנְחָה → *meal offering*, עֹלָה → *burnt offering*, שֶׁלֶם → *peace offerings*, נֶסֶךְ → *drink offerings*, חֹדֶשׁ → *new moons*, מוֹעֵד → *appointed feasts*, מַצָּה → *unleavened bread* and מַשְׁקֶה → *well watered pastures*; it is the noun in חֹק → *the set portion* (45:14) and מְזוּזָה → *the door posts* (45:19), where the ASV's added word is a specifier and the noun carries the lexeme, as the bare *the posts* later in 45:19 confirms.

report: One genuine cross-verse split, and it sits in the `added` units, which the lemma table cannot see. A function word the ASV supplies before a bare Hebrew nominal is aligned to that nominal under rule 33 in 45:1 (*of five and twenty thousand*), 45:11 (*of one measure*), 45:14 (*of the bath*) and 45:23 (*for a sin offering*), but marked `added` in 45:5 (the italic *for* of *for twenty chambers*). Nothing in the source licenses the difference: the numeral phrase there is a bare appositional nominal exactly as the appositional noun of 45:23 is, and rule 33 says such a word is never `added`, an ASV italic being corroboration only under rule 7. Patched 45:5, t028 joining s023 and headed on t029 *twenty*, which is the shape of the 45:1 unit *of five*.

The chapter's other eight `added` units are correct and were left alone. Each supplies something no morpheme can carry: a head noun the Hebrew never writes (*reeds* 45:1, *in length* and *in breadth* 45:2), a lexical subject (*whatsoever* 45:7, rule 17), a lexical verb beside a הָיָה that already holds *it shall be* (*to give* 45:17, rule 20), a clause subordinator (*which* 45:14, rule 55), an appositional *even* standing on a phrase no marker marks (45:14, rule 16's limit), and an object pronoun with no object morpheme (*it* 45:19, rule 44). The line between these and the patched 45:5 case is whether a Hebrew noun stands in the clause to bear the relation the supplied word states.

Candidates checked and rejected as source-licensed rather than splits: הָיָה rendered *shall give* in 45:16, where the verb has no other English, against *it shall be* plus an `added` *to give* in 45:17, where it does; the possessive לְ unrepresented under rule 43 in 45:10 and 45:21 but under rule 40 beside a copular *shall be* in 45:12; לָהֶם as *their* in 45:4 and *unto themselves* in 45:5; בֶּן־בָּקָר fused to *young* while שְׂעִיר עִזִּים splits into *he* and *goat*, rule 30's one-English-word condition deciding both; מֵעַל fused to *from* in 45:9 while אֶל־פְּנֵי splits in 45:7 on the same condition; and every article difference in the 94-occurrence הַ group, each following whether the ASV wrote a *the*, an indefinite article, or a determiner another morpheme licenses.

Construct counting under rule 29 is applied consistently: *the ministers of the sanctuary* (45:4), *the ministers of the house* (45:5), *the possession of the city* (45:6) and *the door posts of the house* (45:19) are read as the arthrous case, each present article taking the *the* before its own word while the construct takes a supplied one, and *the holy oblation* (45:7) as the fronting case, where the anarthrous attributive rendering sends the single *the* to the article. Numeral phrases follow rule 42 the same way in 45:1, 45:3, 45:6 and 45:12: the one written *and* goes to the waw standing between the numerals it joins.

BSB: no genuine error among the 27 disagreements. All three families are documented convention differences. The 19 Td cases are articles on nouns the ASV renders indefinitely (*a homer*, *an ephah*, *a bullock*) or where a demonstrative or possessive is the phrase's one determiner; the 4 R cases are a possessive or dative לְ silenced by the ASV's recasting under rules 40 and 43; the 4 Sp1cs cases are the suffix of אֲדֹנָי, unrendered inside *the Lord*. No accepted edge was changed to improve the rate.

Four conventions recorded and one amendment returned. The amendment rewrites rule 33 to state the boundary this chapter met, which is the boundary the 45:5 error crossed: the supplied function word goes to a noun that is present, and where the ASV supplies the head noun as well, the whole phrase is `added`.
